inputs.original_text:
Look, let’s be entirely clear about what we are seeing here: yet another systemic failure of institutional power and a glaring window into how the state cracks down on marginalized or alternative communities under the guise of public safety. A French abbot, Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), has just been convicted in PARIS, France under a deeply concerning and controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” 

Religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France are right to sound the alarm on this. When the state starts wielding vague, heavy-handed legal tools like a law against "psychological subjection," it almost always ends up disproportionately impacting vulnerable groups and setting a dangerous precedent for institutional overreach. This isn't just an isolated legal proceeding; it’s a reflection of a system that criminalizes non-conformity and wields coercive state power instead of addressing the actual root causes of inequality and institutional imbalance. We need radical structural reform, not vague laws that threaten basic freedoms and target communities under subjective pretexts.
inputs.modified_text:
We cannot ignore what this trial in PARIS, France reveals about the oppressive nature of the state when it wields coercive power against alternative communities. Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), has just been convicted under a deeply concerning and controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” This is a glaring window into systemic overreach and institutional failure.

When the state deploys such vague, heavy-handed legal tools under the guise of public safety, it inevitably targets marginalized groups and criminalizes non-conformity. Religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France are entirely justified in sounding the alarm over this dangerous precedent. Instead of addressing the actual root causes of inequality and institutional imbalance, the establishment relies on subjective pretexts to crush basic freedoms. This case proves that we desperately need radical structural reform, not authoritarian laws that protect elite power structures at the expense of vulnerable communities.
